cards.name: Mac Mini task offloading — dispatch harness (1 step pending: subscription token)
cards.desc:
## What this is
Offload heavy jobs from the MacBook (orchestrator) to the always-on Mac Mini (worker) so the laptop stays fast while multitasking. You type one command on the MacBook, the Mini does the work in the background.

## What we built
- **Dispatch harness** at `~/.claude/mini.sh` (auto-loaded via `~/.zshrc`). Commands:
  - `mini-task "<task>" [remote_dir]` — send a full Claude job to the Mini, runs headless, returns instantly
  - `mini-ls` — list jobs + status (RUNNING / done + exit code)
  - `mini-watch <id>` — live tail a jobs output
  - `mini-log <id>` — full log of a finished job
  - `mini-kill <id>` — stop a job
  - `mini-load` — quick Mini health/CPU glance
- Jobs + logs live on the Mini at `~/mini-tasks/<id>.log`

## Cleanup done on the Mini
- Killed a runaway `gbrain import` (92% CPU, stuck 2.5 days)
- Killed orphaned 7-day dev server + 40+ hung filesystem scans
- Load dropped ~30 -> ~20. Left the 3 live claude sessions alone.

## Auth / billing decision
- Chose **subscription token** (flat-rate, no metered API charges) over the pay-per-token API key.
- Why headless failed at first: SSH + nohup jobs cant read the macOS login Keychain, so claude saw "Not logged in." Fix = export `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from the Minis `~/.env` (harness already does this).

## STILL TO DO (1 step, needs a human)
Run once on the Mini to generate the subscription token (OAuth needs a browser):
1. `ssh mini`
2. `claude setup-token` -> open link -> Approve -> copy token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`)
3. `echo "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=sk-ant-oat01-..." >> ~/.env` then `exit`
4. Then run a test: `mini-task "run uname -a and report the machine" \$HOME`

## Known watch-outs
- Mini disk was ~16 GB free — renders could fill it
- Subscription token shares rate limits with laptop Claude use
- No auto-reaper yet — stale sessions/scans will rebuild; consider a LaunchAgent
